card: Synchronizes default datadir handling between GUI and CLI binaries so choosing a custom directory in the GUI applies universally across the toolchain. Currently, custom GUI datadirs are stored in Qt settings that CLI utilities ignore, leading `bitcoin-cli`, `bitcoin-wallet`, and `bitcoind` to look in standard paths and produce errors or split state unless `-datadir` is passed explicitly. The change enables default datadir paths to redirect via symlinks or plain-text files pointing to external targets, migrates existing GUI configs, and updates the wallet tool to load config files. It builds on the merged #27302.
evidence: Author notes in commit 5864569922: 'This means `bitcoin-cli` and `bitcoin-wallet` will try to use the wrong datadir and show errors if they are called without a -datadir arguments, and `bitcoind` will appear to work but use a different datadir, not loading the same wallets and settings, and downloading blocks into the wrong place.'
Author notes follow-up relationship to bitcoin-core/gui#602 and related inconsistencies identified in #27273.
problem: When users select a custom data directory via the GUI setup screen, the setting is saved to Qt settings (`strDataDir` in config files, plist, or registry) which CLI tools cannot read. As a result, running `bitcoind`, `bitcoin-cli`, or `bitcoin-wallet` without an explicit `-datadir` argument either errors out or silently accesses a completely different datadir, risking duplicate block downloads and inaccessible wallets.
scope_notes: A significant portion of the PR (+282/-40) resides in the Qt intro dialog (`src/qt/intro.cpp`) to handle datadir selection, migration of legacy `strDataDir` Qt settings, and conflict resolution prompts if existing GUI and CLI datadirs disagree.
summary: Aligns the data directory used by GUI and CLI tools by default. Rather than storing custom GUI directory paths in platform-specific Qt settings that CLI tools ignore, the GUI establishes a symlink or fallback text file at the default datadir location pointing to the target directory. It also updates `bitcoin-wallet` and test harnesses to parse config files during initialization.
